hints: A query restricts both an index interval [a,b] and a value interval [c,d].
Keep a frequency tree of values for every array prefix; subtracting two prefixes isolates exactly the queried indices.
Coordinate-compress the array values, then query the count between c and d in the difference of prefix roots b and a-1.
analogy: Two cumulative frequency snapshots let you cancel everything before the requested index range, then count only values in the requested band.
example: For x=[3,2,4,5,1,1,5,3], query indices 2..4 and values 2..4. Those three array values are 2, 4, and 5, so the answer is 2.
algorithm: Coordinate-compress the n array values. Build persistent segment-tree roots root[0..n], where root[i] stores frequencies of values in x[1..i]; create root[i] from root[i-1] by adding x[i]. For a query [a,b] and [c,d], find the compressed value range for c..d and return its count in root[b] minus its count in root[a-1].
correctness: Each prefix root stores exactly the frequencies in its prefix. Subtracting root[a-1] from root[b] therefore leaves exactly the values at indices a through b. A range-count query over values c through d counts precisely the indices satisfying both query inequalities.
complexity: O((n+q) log n) time: n persistent updates and q range-count queries each take O(log n). Space is O(n log n) for the persistent nodes.
